rules.native_mapping: State the product subject, audience, screen job, and primary action before changing native composition.
rules.benefit: Prevents generic polish from obscuring the concrete user problem.
rules.validation_rule: The screen brief names a specific subject, user job, and primary action supported by current-code evidence.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently adapted from Apache-2.0 concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Replace page, hero, and hover concepts with native screens, touch, system navigation, and gestures.

rules.native_mapping: Order native content and actions around one screen job, then preserve the app's platform navigation conventions.
rules.benefit: Reduces cognitive load and makes the next action obvious.
rules.validation_rule: A hierarchy list accounts for every existing action and does not remove a behavior contract.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently adapted from Apache-2.0 concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not express hierarchy as a landing page or browser layout.

rules.native_mapping: Choose at most one product-specific native interaction and run evidence-based critique before and after implementation.
rules.benefit: Adds identity without turning every element into decoration.
rules.validation_rule: The signature interaction improves feedback or comprehension and has a reduced-motion equivalent.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently adapted from Apache-2.0 concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Reject hover-only signatures and browser animation output.

rules.native_mapping: Search the local mobile intelligence catalog and filter results to the detected native framework.
rules.benefit: Surfaces relevant design knowledge without loading unrelated datasets.
rules.validation_rule: Every selected record names the target framework, benefit, and deterministic validation.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently authored catalog informed by MIT-licensed structure; notice retained.
rejection_conditions: Catalog record is not validated for the target
Recommendation depends on a remote service
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Exclude browser stacks, stylesheet systems, and web breakpoints.

rules.native_mapping: Synthesize semantic mobile roles and map logical units to framework-native theme types.
rules.benefit: Makes visual decisions consistent, scalable, and accessible across screens.
rules.validation_rule: Typed platform adapters preserve semantic parity and minimum touch targets.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently authored mobile token guidance; MIT structure acknowledged.
rejection_conditions: Raw values have no proven usage
Change would rename a public token without migration
Physical pixels are treated as shared logical units
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Never emit stylesheet variables, utility classes, or browser units.

rules.native_mapping: Prioritize blocked tasks, semantics, targets, text scaling, RTL, keyboard, safe areas, and compact-to-tablet behavior.
rules.benefit: Focuses redesign effort on usability and reach before decoration.
rules.validation_rule: The plan includes measurable accessibility and adaptive acceptance criteria.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently authored mobile checklist informed by MIT-licensed source organization.
rejection_conditions: Finding is presented as deterministic without evidence
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Reject web-only responsiveness and browser performance checks.

rules.native_mapping: Produce a mobile Design Read that separates what to preserve, improve, and question before editing.
rules.benefit: Protects product identity and prevents arbitrary redesign.
rules.validation_rule: Preserve and improve decisions cite source paths or explicit uncertainties.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently adapted from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rejection_conditions: User requested direct behavior change only
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Remove landing-page, stylesheet, DOM, and web-performance directives.

rules.native_mapping: Set density, contrast, shape, typography, motion, and variance dials for touch-first native screens.
rules.benefit: Makes aesthetic decisions explicit and consistent across implementation.
rules.validation_rule: Each dial maps to native tokens, components, or motion behavior and respects accessibility.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently adapted from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not express dials as stylesheet or viewport settings.

rules.native_mapping: Reject generic decoration, excessive cards, gradients, pills, and motion that do not support the native screen job.
rules.benefit: Improves clarity and distinctive product feel through restraint.
rules.validation_rule: Every nonstandard visual or interaction choice has a user-benefit rationale.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently adapted from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Reject web trend checklists and browser-specific taste rules.

rules.native_mapping: Query a local platform-neutral component-intent catalog before selecting framework-native primitives.
rules.benefit: Reuses proven component contracts without importing incompatible implementation.
rules.validation_rule: The plan lists intent, states, semantics, adaptive behavior, and a native primitive for the target framework.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently authored native routing inspired by MIT-licensed registry capabilities.
rejection_conditions: A registry implementation would replace app behavior
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Never import browser component code into a native project.

rules.native_mapping: Resolve component intent to Material or Cupertino, React Native, SwiftUI, or Material3 primitives with local tokens.
rules.benefit: Keeps interaction behavior and accessibility native to each platform.
rules.validation_rule: Generated plans have no cross-framework imports and cover required states.
rules.legal_treatment: Original cross-platform mapping; MIT registry capability acknowledged.
rejection_conditions: Primitive conflicts with app navigation or theme
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not generate HTML, stylesheet classes, or browser components.

required_project_evidence: React Native detection for registry use
rules.native_mapping: Allow compatible registry metadata only in React Native; other frameworks use the same intent through their own native primitives.
rules.benefit: Provides optional discovery without making the plugin or other frameworks depend on React code.
rules.validation_rule: Registry use is optional, local integration is reviewed, and non-React targets receive native plans only.
rules.legal_treatment: Routing guidance independently authored; MIT notice retained.
rejection_conditions: Target is not React Native and registry output is requested
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Reject browser registry entries and any DOM dependency.

rules.native_mapping: Convert request and local code evidence into component intent and explicit native constraints.
rules.benefit: Makes component generation relevant to the existing product rather than generic.
rules.validation_rule: Intent, constraints, states, invariants, and file scope are all present.
rules.legal_treatment: Concept-only, independently authored; no copied prose or code because source licensing is incomplete.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not call a remote component API or emit browser components.

rules.native_mapping: Generate bounded native composition alternatives and select one against user benefit, platform fit, and risk.
rules.benefit: Creates useful design exploration without uncontrolled implementation.
rules.validation_rule: Alternatives preserve the same behavior contract and explain the selected tradeoff.
rules.legal_treatment: Original local workflow; source architecture used as an unlicensed idea only.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Alternatives must use only native mobile primitives.

rules.native_mapping: Emit bounded integration instructions, then refine against current tokens, semantics, motion, and app architecture.
rules.benefit: Turns design intent into safe implementation guidance.
rules.validation_rule: The refinement changes only approved UI scope and produces a change receipt.
rules.legal_treatment: Original local workflow; no copied source output.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Integration output cannot require a browser or web component library.

rules.native_mapping: Keep state at its proven owner and derive presentation values through the framework's reactive model.
rules.benefit: Reduces stale UI and synchronization bugs during redesign.
rules.validation_rule: No new duplicate state is introduced and existing state-transition tests pass.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently summarized from MIT-declared guidance; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Reject server rendering, hydration, browser cache, and Next-specific rules.

rules.native_mapping: Preserve stable item identity, immutable updates, and event ownership using target-framework idioms.
rules.benefit: Keeps selection, focus, animation, and list state reliable.
rules.validation_rule: Interaction tests retain item identity and callbacks after UI composition changes.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently summarized from MIT-declared guidance; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not apply DOM reconciliation or browser event advice.

rules.native_mapping: Isolate expensive presentation and render typed async states without moving data ownership into visual components.
rules.benefit: Improves responsiveness while preserving data flow.
rules.validation_rule: Loading, empty, error, retry, and populated states remain testable and behavior-equivalent.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently summarized from MIT-declared guidance; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Exclude server components, SSR, and browser fetching guidance.

rules.native_mapping: Translate labeled phases to AnimationController intervals, Animated sequences, SwiftUI phase/state animation, or Compose transitions.
rules.benefit: Makes coordinated native motion understandable and maintainable.
rules.validation_rule: Timeline steps name states, durations, interruption policy, and resting outcome.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently translated from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Never install or emit the source animation runtime.

rules.native_mapping: Use native easing or spring parameters and bounded stagger derived from item order.
rules.benefit: Adds rhythm and feedback without overwhelming content.
rules.validation_rule: Stagger is capped, removed for reduced motion, and does not delay primary actions.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently translated from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Generate only target-framework timing code.

rules.native_mapping: Bind controllers and transitions to native lifecycle, support cancellation or retargeting, and dispose owned resources.
rules.benefit: Prevents leaks, stuck states, and janky interaction.
rules.validation_rule: Motion survives rapid interaction, navigation interruption, and teardown without warnings.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently translated from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not use browser frame loops or source-runtime cleanup APIs.

rules.native_mapping: Represent variants as typed native UI states and map presence to framework-native entrance and exit transitions.
rules.benefit: Keeps animation tied to meaningful application state.
rules.validation_rule: Every variant has a stable resting representation and exit cannot hide required actions.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently translated from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Never install or emit the source motion runtime.

rules.native_mapping: Implement press or drag feedback with native gesture recognition, bounded springs, and an explicit cancellation path.
rules.benefit: Makes touch interaction feel responsive and predictable.
rules.validation_rule: Gesture thresholds, interruption, accessibility alternatives, and system-navigation conflicts are tested.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently translated from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not generate pointer-hover or browser gesture APIs.

rules.native_mapping: Use Hero, measured native shared-element support, matched geometry, or Compose shared transitions only when identity is stable.
rules.benefit: Helps users maintain context across navigation.
rules.validation_rule: Source and destination remain usable without the transition and reduced motion removes spatial travel.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently translated from MIT-licensed concepts; notice retained.
rejection_conditions: Transition is required to understand content
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Use only native shared-transition facilities.

rules.native_mapping: Pass typed loading, empty, error, retry, and populated state into native presentation.
rules.benefit: Makes failure and recovery explicit without coupling UI to backend internals.
rules.validation_rule: All states render in isolated UI tests without a live backend.
rules.legal_treatment: Concept-only and independently authored because the source repository has no license.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not add server actions or a browser data framework.

rules.native_mapping: Keep a small app-facing data boundary and preserve repository, service, and callback ownership during redesign.
rules.benefit: Allows visual iteration without destabilizing backend behavior.
rules.validation_rule: Protected data calls and types retain their signatures after UI changes.
rules.legal_treatment: Concept-only and independently authored because the source repository has no license.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: No backend SDK is added solely for the plugin.

rules.native_mapping: Keep authentication and environment access outside reusable presentation components.
rules.benefit: Prevents UI redesign from leaking secrets or changing security behavior.
rules.validation_rule: Presentation code receives typed state and actions, not credentials or environment access.
rules.legal_treatment: Concept-only and independently authored because the source repository has no license.
rejection_conditions: Secret material is in scan scope
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not introduce server or browser auth plumbing.

rules.native_mapping: Apply measured native list virtualization, stable identity, image sizing or caching, and lightweight row composition in each framework.
rules.benefit: Improves responsiveness and memory use on production screens.
rules.validation_rule: Representative list behavior and interaction state pass tests; performance claims are measured.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently translated from MIT-declared React Native guidance; notice retained.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Reject browser image and virtual-list APIs.

rules.native_mapping: Preserve native navigation destinations and use framework presentation, safe-area, inset, and keyboard primitives.
rules.benefit: Prevents broken back behavior, obscured controls, and non-native modal interaction.
rules.validation_rule: Routes, back behavior, keyboard avoidance, safe areas, and modal dismissal remain verified.
rules.legal_treatment: Broad native lessons independently translated from MIT-declared guidance.
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Do not map mobile navigation to browser routing.

required_project_evidence: React Native or Expo dependency when API-specific
rules.native_mapping: Use first-class React Native or Expo rules only when detected; translate only platform-neutral native quality lessons elsewhere.
rules.benefit: Gives React Native deep support without pretending its APIs are portable.
rules.validation_rule: Expo-only guidance activates only for Expo and other frameworks receive their own native APIs.
rules.legal_treatment: Independently summarized from MIT-declared guidance; notice retained.
rejection_conditions: Expo rule in a bare project
React Native API proposed for another framework
rules.web_runtime_rejection: Exclude React Native Web, DOM, SSR, and browser performance rules.
